CHIEF COMPLAINT
Routine follow-up with chronic medical conditions.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Eugene Walker is a 61-year-old male presenting for routine follow-up. He has a significant history of aortic valve replacement and ascending aortic aneurysm repair performed on 1/22/2013. The patient reports increased fatigue, which he attributes to age or being drained at the end of the day, though he continues to ride his bike 20-30 miles regularly. He previously was able to cycle 40 miles but has not attempted that recently. After long bike rides, he sits down and becomes very tired. He expresses concern about his valve longevity, noting his last stress test was on 9/9/2019, approximately 8 years from his surgery. He was told the valve would last eight years and is now at that timeframe. He requested an echocardiogram to assess his current status. He reports nothing has changed drastically since last visit. He does not follow up at Hopkins regularly, finding it too stressful, and gets follow-ups intermittently at the current clinic. He notes his wife and friends have mentioned he purses his lips when breathing while walking, and he was wondering if this is a bad habit. He denies associated wheezing. He reports a small nodule on his right epididymis that he discovered during self-exam. He is not particularly concerned but wanted to ask the doctor about it. Regarding sleep, he usually gets 6-7 hours per night. He gets out of bed at varying times to be at work by 7am, where he lectures. He tries to work out in the morning and recently has made swim reservations twice a week at 5:45am. He reports he snores a little, but his wife has not mentioned him stopping breathing. He denies depression, describing himself as "a pretty happy guy overall." Recent labs from 4/10/2021 showed alkaline phosphatase elevated at 156, total cholesterol 247, HDL 66, LDL 166, triglycerides 74, TSH normal at 2.68, CBC unremarkable, and vitamin D at 94 (high end of normal). He received COVID-19 vaccination with first dose on 1/15/2021 and second dose on 2/5/2021.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Fatigue noted as described in HPI. Pursed lip breathing observed by wife and friends with no associated wheezing. Reports snoring but wife denies apnea. No other symptoms reviewed.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Aortic valve replacement and ascending aortic aneurysm repair (1/22/2013).

MEDICATIONS
Vitamin D3: 50,000 units on Sundays and 2,000 units on the other six days. Clindamycin prior to dental procedures.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient is employed and lectures, requiring him to be at work by 7am. He exercises regularly, cycling 20-30 miles (previously capable of 40 miles). He has made swim reservations twice weekly at 5:45am. He cycles with a friend named Tyler. He is married. He is described as generally happy.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
General: Overall doing well. Respiratory: Pursed lip breathing noted, low exhalation phase, clear to auscultation, no wheezing. Genitalia: Right testicle with 2-3mm palpable nodule that does not appear to involve epididymis or varicocele; left testicle normal; no hernia. All other portions of physical exam normal.

RESULTS
Labs from 4/10/2021: Alkaline phosphatase 156 (elevated), Total cholesterol 247, HDL 66, LDL 166, Triglycerides 74, TSH 2.68 (normal), CBC unremarkable, Vitamin D 94 (high end of normal). Stress test from 9/9/2019.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
History of aortic valve replacement and ascending aortic aneurysm repair: Patient is doing well overall and asymptomatic. Not currently seen by cardiology routinely. Will order echocardiogram and stress test. Recommend follow-up with cardiology, Dr. Vincent Sanchez suggested as physician. Elevated alkaline phosphatase level: Most recent level 156, likely related to bone health but could be related to liver. Will order alkaline phosphatase and GGT labs today. Results will be sent through patient portal unless abnormal, then will call patient. Pursed lip breathing and fatigue: Patient noted to have pursed lip breathing with low exhalation phase on examination. Despite fatigue, continues to be active with cycling 20-30 miles. Will order pulmonary function tests for further evaluation. Right testicular nodule: 2-3mm palpable nodule noted on examination. Will place urology referral for possible ultrasound. Preventive health: MMR vaccine to be administered today. Shingles vaccine recommended, to be arranged by front desk for next month. COVID-19 vaccination complete. Follow-up: Patient to return in one year for wellness visit. Will review sooner if needed after all labs and studies are completed. Patient to call with any questions or concerns.
